Stump grinding in Davenport typically runs $150–$500 per stump, with big stumps — like the trunk of a mature EAB-killed ash — reaching $300–$800. It is almost never included in a tree removal quote by default, which is why yards across the city carry a stump for every removal that stopped at the flush cut. Two things set the price: diameter (the wheel works the face of the stump, so area is time) and access. One thing sets the safety: the free Iowa One Call 811 utility locate that must happen before any grinding.

Sources: Angi / HomeGuide / homeyou 2026 cost data; local contractor pricing ranges; Iowa One Call (811)

Below the grass line

A grinder chews the stump into chips 6–12 inches below grade — enough to mow over, seed, or lay sod. Grinding deeper for a replant in the same spot costs more but is routine. What grinding does not do is remove the root system: the buried roots decay in place over several years, which is normal and harmless. The mound of chips left behind settles as it decomposes; topping the hole with soil after a season is standard.

The one thing that must happen before any grinding: a utility locate. Gas services, buried electric, irrigation, and cable routinely run near old trees, and a grinder wheel does not care what it hits. Iowa One Call (811) locates are free and required — a crew that shrugs at this question is telling you something. Also mention any known obstacles: old fence posts, landscape lighting runs, or a previous stump's leftover hardware.

  • Ground 6–12 inches below grade — deeper on request for replanting
  • 811 utility locate before the wheel touches dirt
  • Chips left as fill or hauled — your call
  • Multi-stump discounts: batching is genuinely cheaper per stump

Davenport Stump Grinding — FAQ

Why isn't the stump included in my removal quote?
Different machine, different trip, sometimes a different crew — so most companies price it separately, and many homeowners skip it at removal time. Ask for the stump price in the same written quote so you can decide with real numbers. Batching the stump with the removal is almost always cheaper than calling someone back later.
Grinding vs. full stump removal — which do I need?
Grinding, in nearly every residential case. Digging a stump out whole — roots and all — costs several times more and tears up the yard, and is only genuinely needed for construction, foundations, or hardscape going in that exact spot. For a lawn, grinding below grade gives the same end result.
Will the tree grow back from the stump?
Some species resprout from the stump and roots — silver maple, willow, and boxelder will try. Grinding removes the crown tissue most regrowth starts from, and mowing off any root suckers that appear the first season finishes the job. Ash killed by EAB does not come back.
Can you grind a stump close to my foundation or fence?
Usually — grinders are maneuverable, and the wheel can work within inches of hardscape. Very tight access (narrow gates, steep slopes) may need a smaller machine, which is worth mentioning when you ask for the quote so the right equipment shows up.
